claimLedger.wording: Plumby is made by Ordinary Nerds, L.L.C. and distributed at plumby.app.
claimLedger.excerpt: a legal agreement between you and Ordinary Nerds, L.L.C. ... for the Plumby software

claimLedger.wording: The vendor documents macOS 15 or later on Apple silicon and Intel.

claimLedger.conditions: Compatibility claim, not installed/tested hardware evidence

claimLedger.wording: Plumby advertises free scans and explanations, with a non-expiring allowance of 5 GB clearing and 3 full app removals.
claimLedger.excerpt: Scanning, measuring, and viewing what is on your Mac are unmetered ... 5 GB cleared ... 3 apps fully removed
claimLedger.conditions: Separate allowances; EULA says installed version sets allowances and changes are not retroactive. No account or credit card; not an expiring trial.

claimLedger.wording: The advertised prices are US$29/year or US$79 once, covering 2 Macs; applicable tax is additional as charged at checkout.
claimLedger.excerpt: Plumby Annual — $29/year (USD) ... Plumby Lifetime — $79 one-time (USD) ... 2 Macs per license
supportingExcerpts: The price is the one shown on the pricing page and at checkout when you buy, together with any tax your country charges.
The launch price of $19/year and $59 lifetime ended on 30 September 2026
claimLedger.conditions: Advertised, no checkout opened or price paid. Recheck within 30 days and before publication. Do not reuse ended launch offer.

claimLedger.wording: Annual renews automatically every 12 months; after cancellation the installed version keeps working but updates stop at the end of the paid year. Lifetime includes future versions. Refunds are offered within 14 days of a payment.
claimLedger.excerpt: renews automatically every 12 months ... Your installed version of Plumby keeps working ... Updates stop at the end of the year you have paid for ... Any payment can be refunded within 14 days
claimLedger.conditions: Not a tested cancellation/refund; refund revokes the paid key, unlike cancellation

claimLedger.wording: Plumby uses a proprietary personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable licence; the EULA restricts redistribution and reverse engineering subject to applicable law.
claimLedger.excerpt: personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable ... may not ... redistribute the Software ... All rights, title, and intellectual property ... remain with Ordinary Nerds, L.L.C.

claimLedger.wording: The vendor documents manual review plus optional scheduled Quick Plunge, off until enabled; it is not accurate to say every cleanup always needs a fresh approval.
claimLedger.excerpt: Quick Plunge can run on a schedule — daily, weekly or monthly — and it is off until you turn it on. A scheduled run clears by itself, without asking each time, and only when it would free at least half a gigabyte.
claimLedger.conditions: Unversioned EULA; exact eligible paths/methods not established. Do not repeat homepage-only blanket approval wording.

claimLedger.wording: The homepage groups removal consequences, including a separately reviewed old iPhone backup, but official pages disagree about its removal method.
claimLedger.excerpt: An old iPhone backup can’t be put back, so Plumby shows it on its own, with its date, before anything happens.
claimLedger.conflictingExcerpt: Big old files, iPhone backups and installers go to the macOS Trash, where Finder's Put Back returns them, and no setting can change that.
claimLedger.conditions: EULA section 5 gives general own-files-to-Trash rules, but does not resolve the iPhone-backup-specific contradiction. No operational recommendation until version-specific resolution.

claimLedger.wording: Plumby documents disk breakdown, app uninstall/leftovers, running-app use, menu-bar readings and checkups.
claimLedger.excerpt: Disk breakdown ... Uninstall completely ... Running now ... In the menu bar ... Memory, battery and storage, one click away.
claimLedger.conditions: No speed, complete uninstallation or memory-boost effectiveness verified. Nine checkup areas on features page vs 26 checks on homepage need not be inconsistent; do not conflate areas with test count.

claimLedger.wording: Plumby's policy says analysis runs locally, while licence/update checks and feature-specific requests can leave the Mac; Ask requires Apple Intelligence.
claimLedger.excerpt: Plumby analyses your Mac locally ... Some things do leave your Mac ... a licence check, an update check ... lookups that only run when you open the feature that needs them
supportingExcerpts: Ask is available only on Macs with Apple Intelligence turned on. Questions and answers stay on your Mac.
claimLedger.conditions: No blanket offline/no-network guarantee. Policy includes website advertising and an inconsistent later no-targeted-advertising sentence: do not certify privacy compliance or repeat that negative claim.

claimLedger.wording: Plumby is offered by direct download, advertised as Apple-notarized. Full Disk Access expands inspection; helper approval is required for fan control and password-free maintenance.

supportingExcerpts: It works without it, and tells you which places it could not check.
It ships directly instead, notarized by Apple before it reaches you.

workflowArticle.proposedTitle: Make room for a macOS update without confusing Trash with free space
workflowArticle.primaryIntent: Decide which files to review before an OS update, distinguish item size, permanent removal, Trash occupancy and actual available space; Plumby's consequence labels are the concrete comparison case.
workflowArticle.descriptionDirection: Conclusion first: use a review list and check available space separately; do not treat illustrated update thresholds or selected-byte totals as universal installation requirements.
sections: Read consequences before adding sizes (P08; blocked until resolved)
Separate rebuildable data, personal copies and backups
Trash movement is not newly available storage
Compare Plumby's labels with Breathing Room's source-level owner/project views (P09/B02)
Choose a tool by permissions, version, local/hosted boundary and support needs
workflowArticle.visualPlan: Lead: official Plumby Overview only after clearance. Later: selected BR Space browser preview with required caption. Optional decision checklist does not replace app screenshot.
workflowArticle.interactionHandoff: Non-mutating checklist: backup exists? only copy? rebuild/redownload cost? actual removal method? Trash not emptied? required available-space amount confirmed for this specific update? No delete buttons or fake scanner.
workflowArticle.boundaries: No invented Apple storage requirement, benchmark, native test or steps for irreversible backups. Any OS-update requirement needs official version-specific Apple documentation during drafting. No runnable cleanup demo. No draft until blockers resolve.
workflowArticle.distinctness: Workflow explains consequence-aware update preparation, not an expanded feature matrix; proposed slug only, collision audit pending in drafting scope.
